Neil deGrasse Tyson joins the Joe Rogan Experience for episode 1904, a full-length visit after many short clips. Tyson, director of the Hayden Planetarium and host of StarTalk, is America's most famous astronomy teacher. Rogan gives him the long format to teach at his own pace.

He schools Rogan, his word and his manner, on space, science, and the state of wonder in a distracted age. The talk moves from black holes to science funding to the words we use for the sky. The episode is a cosmic class with jokes, taught by a man who believes awe is a civic duty.
podcast-joerogan-inrnVpGsKN4:
Comedian Tony Hinchcliffe joins Joe Rogan for episode 2522. Hinchcliffe hosts Kill Tony, the live roast and open-mic hit. His jokes are sharp, fast, and often brutal.

Rogan and Hinchcliffe trade tales from Austin's comedy boom. They discuss young comics, roasts, and the risks of raw humor. Hinchcliffe defends his style against its many critics. The talk stays funny even when the subject turns grave. Listeners get two comedy insiders on the scene they helped build, with no punches pulled for the audience at home. The roasts discussed here spare almost no one.
podcast-joerogan-oQrsGjT0Sn4:
Steven Hassan, an author and counselor who works with former cult members, talks with Joe Rogan in episode 680. Hassan once belonged to the Unification Church, often called the Moonies, before leaving. Since then he has spent decades studying how groups control people's minds.

Hassan explains the warning signs of a controlling group, from love bombing to cutting off outside views. He shares stories from his own years inside and from people he has helped leave. Rogan asks how the same tactics show up in politics and online life. The talk works as a clear field guide to mind control.
podcast-joerogan-oU-AQ2Rfmn4:
Jordan Peterson, the Canadian psychologist and author, returns to the Joe Rogan Experience for episode 1933. Peterson is known for lectures on meaning, order, and personal duty that drew a huge online following. His Rogan talks are long, dense, and wide-ranging by habit.

The two move through culture, faith, and the fights around speech and gender that made Peterson famous and divisive. Peterson explains his view that people need rules and aims to keep chaos at bay. Rogan tests the ideas with stories from comedy and fighting. Fans get the full Peterson treatment, given room to breathe.
podcast-tuckercarlson-dbLHXOipQN4:
Crypto pioneer Roger Ver joins Tucker Carlson while facing extradition from Spain. Carlson lays out the charge: tax evasion with a possible 109-year term. Ver is not an American citizen for the years in dispute.

Carlson says such cases set off his alarm at once. The title argues that spy agencies want every transaction tracked. It frames Ver's case as a test of cash and privacy. Ver tells his side of a fight with the tax arm of the state. The episode warns savers that money trails may be the point.
